description: How financial institutions meet their legal obligations and how technology automates the work: why financial regulation exists, know your customer and anti-money laundering, data protection law, reporting to regulators, automated compliance monitoring, regulatory sandboxes and risk management frameworks, with the Bank of Ghana and other African regulators as the running cases. Students build compliance tools in the browser, including a KYC onboarding flow, a transaction monitoring engine and a machine-readable regulatory return, and test them against simulated customers and transactions.
modelledOn: FATF Recommendations on combating money laundering and the financing of terrorism
Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, Basel III framework
ISO 31000 Risk Management and the COSO Enterprise Risk Management framework
Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialist (CAMS) body of knowledge
outcomes: Explain why financial regulation exists, the roles of central banks and other regulators, and the main regulatory objectives.
Design know-your-customer and customer due diligence processes that follow a risk-based approach.
Build anti-money laundering controls, including sanctions screening and transaction monitoring, and evaluate their accuracy.
Apply data protection law to the design of financial systems and the handling of personal data.
Automate regulatory reporting and compliance monitoring and explain the use of SupTech by regulators.
Apply risk management frameworks and assess innovations through a regulatory sandbox.

units.title: Financial regulation and why it exists
topics: Market failures that justify regulation: information asymmetry, systemic risk, contagion and consumer harm
Objectives of regulation: financial stability, consumer protection, market integrity and financial inclusion
Regulators and their mandates: the Bank of Ghana, the Securities and Exchange Commission, the National Insurance Commission; central banks across Africa
Prudential regulation: capital adequacy, liquidity and the Basel accords; conduct regulation
Lessons from crises: the 2008 global crisis and Ghana's 2017 to 2019 banking sector clean-up
What RegTech and SupTech are: automating compliance for firms and supervision for regulators

units.title: Know your customer
topics: Customer due diligence: identification, verification, beneficial ownership and the purpose of the relationship
Risk-based approach: simplified, standard and enhanced due diligence; politically exposed persons
Digital identity and e-KYC: the Ghana Card and the national identification system, biometric and document verification, liveness checks
Tiered KYC for mobile money and financial inclusion; balancing access and risk
Building a KYC onboarding flow with identity checks and a customer risk score

units.title: Anti-money laundering and countering terrorist financing
topics: Money laundering stages (placement, layering, integration) and terrorist financing; typologies in mobile money and trade
The FATF Recommendations, mutual evaluations and grey listing; Ghana's AML/CFT law and the Financial Intelligence Centre
Sanctions screening: sanctions lists, fuzzy name matching, transliteration and managing false positives
Suspicious transaction reports, cash transaction reports and record keeping
Correspondent banking, de-risking and its effect on remittances to Africa
Crypto-assets and virtual asset service providers; the travel rule

units.title: Data protection law
topics: Principles of data protection: lawfulness, purpose limitation, minimisation, accuracy, storage limitation, security and accountability
Ghana's Data Protection Act 2012 (Act 843) and the Data Protection Commission; registration of data controllers
Comparing the EU GDPR, Kenya's Data Protection Act, Nigeria's Data Protection Act and the African Union Malabo Convention
Data subject rights, consent, cross-border data transfers and data localisation rules
Privacy by design: data protection impact assessments, pseudonymisation, encryption and retention schedules
Breach notification and the tension between data protection and KYC record-keeping obligations

units.title: Reporting to regulators
topics: Prudential returns: capital, liquidity, large exposures and asset quality; reporting calendars
Electronic reporting systems such as the Bank of Ghana's Online Regulatory and Analytical Surveillance Software
Data standards for reporting: XBRL, data dictionaries and granular data collection
Machine-readable and machine-executable regulation; regulation as code
Data quality, lineage and reconciliation between source systems and returns
Generating and validating a regulatory return from a simulated loan book

units.title: Automated compliance monitoring
topics: Transaction monitoring: rule-based scenarios, thresholds, structuring and velocity rules
Machine learning for anomaly detection and alert scoring; network analysis of money flows
Measuring a monitoring system: precision, recall, false positive rates and alert backlogs
Explainability, model governance and audit trails for automated decisions
Case management workflows and evidence for investigators
Building a transaction monitoring engine and tuning it against simulated mobile money fraud and laundering

units.title: Regulatory sandboxes
topics: Why sandboxes exist: testing innovation under supervision with limits on customers and exposure
Sandbox design: eligibility, testing parameters, safeguards, exit criteria and reporting
The Bank of Ghana regulatory and innovation sandbox and sandboxes in Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda and Sierra Leone
Innovation hubs, test-and-learn approaches and cross-border sandbox networks
Preparing a sandbox application for a fintech product

units.title: Risk management frameworks
topics: Enterprise risk management with ISO 31000 and COSO: risk identification, assessment, treatment and monitoring
Risk categories: credit, market, liquidity, operational, compliance and reputational risk
The three lines model, risk appetite statements, key risk indicators and risk registers
Operational and cyber risk: the Bank of Ghana Cyber and Information Security Directive, business continuity
Third-party and outsourcing risk, including cloud providers and agent networks

units.title: Governance, ethics and capstone
topics: Compliance governance: the compliance officer, board oversight, internal audit and whistleblowing
Ethics and culture: conflicts of interest, fair treatment of customers and responsible use of data
Choosing and integrating RegTech vendors; build versus buy
Capstone: a compliance platform for a mobile money provider covering KYC, monitoring, reporting and a risk register

schedule.title: Why regulation exists
schedule.exercise: Pick one market failure (information asymmetry, systemic risk or consumer harm) and explain with a Ghanaian example how regulation addresses it.

tasks.title: Match four regulatory objectives (stability, consumer protection, market integrity, inclusion) to the rule that best serves each, with reasons
Decide which regulator (Bank of Ghana, Securities and Exchange Commission, National Insurance Commission) should handle five described complaints
Explain, for a described market failure scenario, which objective of regulation it threatens and why unregulated firms would not fix it alone

schedule.title: Prudential and conduct regulation
schedule.exercise: Summarise one lesson from Ghana's 2017 to 2019 banking sector clean-up and state the rule change it led to.

tasks.title: Decide whether three described rules are prudential or conduct regulation, and explain what failure each is meant to prevent
Read a short account of a bank failure and identify the capital or liquidity weakness that a Basel-style rule would have caught earlier
Explain, for a described compliance task, whether RegTech or SupTech would help more, and sketch what it would automate
Assess a bank's capital and liquidity position against a stated requirement and decide whether it would pass or fail, with the numbers shown

schedule.title: Customer due diligence and digital identity
schedule.exercise: Design a tiered KYC table for a mobile money service showing what identification is needed at three transaction limits, and explain why a politically exposed person needs enhanced checks.

tasks.title: Review a customer onboarding case and decide what identification, verification and beneficial ownership information is still missing
Verify a simulated Ghana Card identity check against a liveness check and decide whether the onboarding should pass, need review, or be declined
Build a KYC onboarding flow with identity checks and a risk score for five simulated customers, and justify the resulting risk tier for each

schedule.title: Money laundering and sanctions screening
schedule.exercise: Explain the three stages of money laundering with one mobile money example of each stage.

tasks.title: Classify five simulated transaction patterns as placement, layering or integration, and justify each classification
Screen a batch of customer names against a sanctions list with fuzzy matching, and decide which of three partial matches are true hits
Assess whether a simulated country's AML/CFT weaknesses described in a short brief would risk a grey listing, and recommend one priority fix

schedule.title: Reporting obligations and emerging risks
schedule.exercise: Write the criteria you would use to decide whether a transaction pattern merits a suspicious transaction report.

tasks.title: Decide, for five simulated transactions, which require a suspicious transaction report or a cash transaction report, and draft one report
Assess how a correspondent bank's de-risking decision would affect a remittance corridor into Ghana, and propose one mitigation
Decide what additional checks a virtual asset service provider must apply under the travel rule for a described cross-border transfer

schedule.title: Data protection principles
schedule.exercise: Write a short note applying the principles of lawfulness, purpose limitation and minimisation to a mobile money data collection form.

tasks.title: Review a data collection form against the data protection principles and flag two fields that breach purpose limitation or minimisation
Decide whether a described data controller must register under Ghana's Data Protection Act 843, and list the obligations that follow
Compare Ghana's Act 843 with the GDPR on one chosen principle, and state the practical difference for a company operating in both markets

schedule.title: Data subject rights and privacy by design
schedule.exercise: Design a data protection impact assessment outline for a new mobile money feature that shares location data with merchants.

tasks.title: Run a data protection impact assessment on a described new feature, identifying the privacy risk and the mitigation (pseudonymisation, encryption, retention)
Decide whether a described cross-border data transfer is permitted under Ghana's rules, and what safeguard would make a borderline case acceptable
Resolve a conflict between a data subject's erasure request and a KYC record-keeping obligation, and justify which rule prevails and why

schedule.title: Regulatory reporting and data standards
schedule.exercise: Explain, with an example field, how an ISO 20022 or XBRL tag turns a bank's internal figure into a machine-readable regulatory submission.

tasks.title: Prepare a prudential return's capital and liquidity figures from a simulated bank's ledger and check them against the reporting template
Tag three figures from a bank's return with the matching data dictionary codes, and flag one figure that does not match any defined tag
Generate a regulatory return from a simulated loan book, validate it against two consistency rules, and correct one flagged discrepancy

schedule.title: Transaction monitoring
schedule.exercise: Design three rule-based scenarios (thresholds, structuring, velocity) for monitoring mobile money transactions, and state what each is meant to catch.

tasks.title: Write threshold and velocity monitoring rules in SQL against a transaction table and report how many simulated accounts they flag
Review an anomaly-scored alert from a described network analysis of money flows and decide whether it warrants escalation
Measure the precision and recall of a tuned monitoring rule set against a labelled sample of simulated transactions, and adjust one threshold to cut false positives

schedule.title: Governance of automated decisions
schedule.exercise: Write the case file structure an investigator would need to review an automated alert, including what explanation the system must provide.

tasks.title: Review an automated transaction-monitoring decision and decide what audit trail and explanation it must produce to satisfy a model governance rule
Build a case management workflow for a flagged alert, from assignment through evidence gathering to a closing decision
Tune a transaction monitoring engine against a simulated set of mobile money fraud and laundering cases, and report the change in false positives after tuning

schedule.title: Regulatory sandboxes
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page sandbox application for a fictional fintech product, covering eligibility, testing limits, safeguards and exit criteria.

tasks.title: Design the eligibility criteria, testing limits and exit criteria for a sandbox cohort of three fintech applicants
Compare the Bank of Ghana's regulatory sandbox with one other African country's sandbox and recommend one feature Ghana's could adopt
Prepare a sandbox application for a described fintech product, defending the testing parameters and safeguards against a reviewer's questions

schedule.title: Enterprise and operational risk
schedule.exercise: Build a risk register with five entries for a mobile money provider, each with a category, likelihood, impact and a key risk indicator.

tasks.title: Classify five described risk events by category (credit, market, liquidity, operational, compliance, reputational) and justify two borderline cases
Write a risk appetite statement and three key risk indicators for a described mobile money provider, and justify the thresholds chosen
Assess the outsourcing risk of a described cloud provider and agent network, and propose the contractual safeguard that most reduces it

schedule.title: Compliance governance capstone
schedule.exercise: Design a compliance platform outline for a mobile money provider covering KYC, monitoring, reporting and a risk register, and justify one build-versus-buy decision in it.

tasks.title: Decide who should have final sign-off (compliance officer, board, internal audit) for three described compliance decisions, and justify each
Compare two RegTech vendor options for a described compliance need and justify a build-versus-buy recommendation
Build a compliance platform outline for a mobile money provider covering KYC, monitoring, reporting and a risk register, scored on a capstone rubric
